## Background

::: {.panel-tabset}

### Minimum

*Not written yet.*

### Medium

Reactions are represented by initial value problems. For example, the initial
value problem for [Example 3: Hydrogen peroxide catalase](../../index.qmd#sec-hydrogen-peroxide-catalase) is
$$
\begin{aligned}
    E'(t) &= -k_1 E\ S + k_2 X\ S - k_3 E, &E(0)= E_0\\
    S'(t) &= -K_1 E\ S - k_2 X\ S, &S(0) = S_0\\
    X'(t) &= K_1 E\ S - k_2 X\ S, &X(0) = X_0\\
    P'(t) &= k_2 X\ S, &P(0) = P_0\\
    I'(t) &= k_3 E, &I(0) = 0
\end{aligned}
$$
where

* $E$ = the concentration of the catalase
* $S$ = the concentration of hydrogen peroxide
* $X$ = the concentration of an enzyme-substrate complex formed during the reaction of hydrogen peroxide and the catalase
* $P$ = the concentration of the product formation (?) of ???
* $I$ = the concentration of an inactive form of the catalase

and $k_1$, $k_2$, and $k_3$ are the rates of the reactions.

These equations are created in a similar manner to compartment models. We begin
with the simplest example, $A \to B$, from the
[Reaction equations](../../index.qmd#eq-simple-reaction) page.
